Simulated DH genotype data for multivariate QTL mapping

Source: R/genoMVsim.R
genoMVsim.Rd

A simulated Doubled Haploid (DH) mapping population for use in the multivariate QTL mapping vignette. The population consists of 120 DH lines genotyped at 100 markers on each of 6 chromosomes (600 markers total) at 1 cM spacing, giving 594 marker intervals.

The object is of class "bc" as produced by qtl::sim.cross() and is intended to be passed directly to primeCross().

Four QTL were planted at the following positions:

Chr1, interval 20

Main effect — consistent positive effect across all eight trials.

Chr3, interval 40

Main effect — consistent negative effect across all eight trials.

Chr2, interval 55

G×E interaction — strong positive effect in early trials, fading to near zero by trial 8.

Chr5, interval 70

G×E interaction — symmetric crossover: negative in trials 1–4, positive in trials 5–8.

Usage

genoMVsim

Format

An object of class c("bc", "cross") with components:

$geno

Named list of 6 chromosome objects, each containing $data (marker genotype matrix) and $map (cM positions).

$pheno

Data frame with columns id (line identifier) and phenotype (placeholder; phenotypic data are in phenoMVsim).

See also

phenoMVsim, primeCross, qtlAim

Examples

data(genoMVsim, package = "wgAim")
length(genoMVsim$geno)       # 6 chromosomes
#> [1] 6
nmar(genoMVsim)              # 100 markers per chromosome
#> Chr1 Chr2 Chr3 Chr4 Chr5 Chr6 
#>  100  100  100  100  100  100
